newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa eases further as selling continues.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa eases further as selling continues.

text.p: Cocoa futures continued to run into fresh selling and long liquidation on Tuesday as the market came under further pressure after Monday's fund-led sell-off.
By midsession, the benchmark contract lost 12 stg at 973 stg a tonne after ranging between 972 and 985 stg. It had gapped three stg down more or less in line with pre-market expectations.
"The market is still under pressure," said one trader. "The structure has also weakened."
Analysts said the only constructive factor on Monday was that London closed above a key uptrend and support at 980 stg, despite dipping below that level earlier in the day.
Apparently, that support had been taken out and others were now pegging initial support at 960 to the mid-February trough of 895 stg.
There was no fundamental news behind the move, which has sliced values by 4.2 percent in two days.
On Monday, speculators relentlessly unloaded their long positions after the market posted a key chart reversal.

The heavy liquidation was reflected in Tuesday's data which showed a fall of 3,583 lots in uncovered September positions to 17,968 as at the close of business on Monday. But the March position showed a rise of 1,225 to 35,013.
"Many people were getting out of the market," the trader said.
Sept/Dec switches were traded at 35-36 stg against up to 37 on Monday. On Friday, the switches were actively traded at 10 stg.
On the fundamental front, broker GNI said it believed that a crop in excess of 1.2 million tonnes is possible for Ivory Coast next year if favourable conditions remain through November.
